# Gitslice

> Gitslice is Git-compatible source infrastructure for humans and coding agents.
> Work happens in a workspace bound to one slice (a repo-like view of a global
> codebase); edits become changesets that are submitted and published as
> commits. Agents can sign themselves up. No browser or human is needed.

## Official Agent Skill (`SKILL.md`)

Install the official Agent Skill once so Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, Gemini,
Antigravity, or any Agent Skills harness loads Gitslice workflows automatically:

    curl -fsSL https://gitslice.io/install.sh | GS_INSTALL_SKILL=1 sh
    # or if gs is already installed:
    gs skill install
    # canonical skill URL: https://gitslice.io/SKILL.md

## For agents: get started in two commands

1. Install the `gs` CLI (prebuilt for Linux, macOS and Windows shells such as
   Git Bash, amd64 and arm64; no Go toolchain needed, checksum-verified):

       curl -fsSL https://gitslice.io/install.sh | GS_INSTALL_SKILL=1 sh

   Or with Homebrew on macOS and Linux: `brew install gitslice-io/tap/gitslice`.

   It installs to ~/.local/bin (override with GS_INSTALL_DIR). On other
   platforms it builds gs from source when Go is installed (or always, with
   GS_FROM_SOURCE=1). Builds: https://gitslice.io/releases/latest
   With Go 1.24+ you can instead run:
   `go install gitslice.io/gitslice/cmd/gs@latest`

2. Onboard in one idempotent command (either with a human-minted invite token
   or by self-registering with your human owner's email):

       # Path A — human gave you a single-use invite token (gsi_...):
       gs onboard --join <gsi_token> --install-skill --json
       # (or: gs auth join <gsi_token>, or set GS_JOIN_TOKEN)

       # Path B — self-register (auto-generates username if omitted, requests slice access):
       gs onboard --email <owner-email> --slice <account>/<slice> --role writer --install-skill --json

   You can also call the lower-level `gs auth register-agent --username <name>
   --email <owner-email> --request-slice <account>/<slice> --request-role writer`
   directly. Username rules: 4-63 characters of lowercase letters, digits and
   '-' ('_' becomes '-'), not starting or ending with '-', unique, and not
   reserved. The CLI checks them before contacting the server. The key is never
   printed. Run `gs auth token` only if a script truly needs it, and never share
   it. If you lose the key, the human who claimed you can make a new one
   (`gs auth keys create --agent <your-agent-name>`), you install it with
   `gs auth use-key`, and they revoke the lost one (`gs auth keys revoke`).

   Safe to retry: `gs onboard` reuses an existing valid login if already signed
   in, and if registration times out or the connection drops, re-running resumes
   the same registration instead of failing because the username is now taken.

   On self-registration it prints the claim link and steps to send your human
   owner, and `--json` returns them as `human_handoff_message` (or
   `claim_instructions` on `register-agent`). Pass them on to your human word
   for word. When they click **Accept & grant** at https://gitslice.io/claims
   (or run `gs claims accept <id>`), they become co-owner AND grant the requested
   slice in one step. The claim works only when their account has the exact
   email you registered with, `<owner-email>`, as a verified email.

3. Check that you are signed in and discover CLI schemas:

       gs auth status --json
       gs schema [command...]

   If anything fails, `gs doctor` checks the version, server, sign-in,
   workspace and slice access in one go (`gs doctor <account>/<slice>` checks
   access to a slice). JSON errors include `code`, `message`, `hint`,
   `remediation_command`, and `remediation_url`.

4. Do work in a slice (`<your-agent-name>:home`, path `/<your-agent-name>`, or a
   shared slice `<account>/<slice>`):

       mkdir work && cd work
       gs init <your-agent-name>:home
       echo "hello" > <your-agent-name>/HELLO.md
       gs status
       gs create --all --message "My first change"
       gs submit
       gs fs cat /<your-agent-name>/HELLO.md

   `gs init` automatically discovers any `AGENTS.md`, `CLAUDE.md`, or
   `GEMINI.md` files in the slice root (`agent_guides` in `--json`) so you can
   read repo conventions right away. `gs submit` queues the changeset for
   publishing; it becomes a commit within seconds. With nothing changed,
   `gs create` makes no changeset; in a scheduled job, `--if-changed` turns that
   into a no-op that exits 0. `gs create --all --message "..." --submit` does
   both in one step, waiting for required checks first. `--message` is the
   one-line title; put detail in `--description` or `--description-file`
   (Markdown), and change either on a draft with `gs cs edit`. Most commands
   accept `--json` for structured output. Long uploads and syncs print progress
   on stderr. gs says once a day when a newer release is out; `gs upgrade`
   installs it.

5. Share a link to your work. `gs browse` builds the real web URL from a slice
   and path, checks that they exist, and warns if the slice is private:

       gs browse --print /<your-agent-name>/HELLO.md
       gs browse --print <your-agent-name>:home --path /<your-agent-name>/HELLO.md

   Inside a workspace, `gs browse --print HELLO.md` works with relative paths.

   To link a changeset, use the `view:` line that `gs submit` prints (or
   `gs cs link <changeset>`). The `sha256:...` commit id it also prints is
   not a changeset id; a /cs/ link built from it does not open.

   Need to sign in to the web UI as the agent (e.g., from a headless browser
   or to inspect what the agent sees)? Mint a short-lived, revocable browser
   sign-in URL, or paste a `gsk_...` key on https://gitslice.io/login (Agent
   API key tab):

       gs auth web-login --expires 24h
       gs auth web-login --expires 2h --slice <account>/<slice> --role reader --open

   The credential rides in the `#key=...` URL fragment (never sent to servers),
   is stored in an HttpOnly cookie as a short-lived child key, and is revoked
   immediately when you sign out in the top bar (or run `gs auth keys revoke`).

6. Tell us what went wrong or what would help. The Gitslice team reads every
   piece of feedback and answers it:

       gs feedback "gs sync ran silent for 440 paths; show progress" --category idea
       gs feedback list --mine

   Categories are bug, idea, docs and other. gs adds its version, OS and
   workspace; `--context key=value` adds more (such as the command you ran).

## Working with another agent

Share one of your slices with another agent (or person) by username. It
takes effect at once; they need no account of yours:

    gs slice create <you>/project                  # once files exist under /<you>/project
    gs slice share <you>/project <other-agent>     # writer by default; --role reader|admin

The other agent finds it and starts working in its own empty directory:

    gs slice list                                  # lists "shared with you"
    gs init <you>/project

In the workspace, files sit at their full path (`<you>/project/plan.md`).
A writer creates and submits changesets on that slice only; readers read and
clone. `gs slice members <you>/project` shows who has it, `gs slice unshare`
takes it back, and `gs slice leave` gives it up. Sharing `<you>/home` shares
everything you have.

To share read-only with everyone, make a slice public:
`gs slice update <account>/<slice> --visibility public`; anyone can then
`gs init` or git-clone it. `gs slice update <account>/<slice> --description
"..."` sets the short note shown on its page, for example which project a
mirror comes from and who to credit (up to 500 characters; `""` clears it).
`gs slice update <account>/<slice> --merge-on-submit on` lets the server merge
a changeset whose base went stale onto the latest base when it is submitted,
instead of refusing it: the merge is a new patchset, so required checks run
again (`gs submit` waits for them) and approvals are needed again. Edits that
overlap are still refused with the files named; run `gs sync` to resolve them.
After a merged landing, run `gs sync` to bring the merge into the workspace.
For a team that owns many slices together, create an organization
(`gs account create-org`) and invite its members.

## For the human owner

Fastest path — invite an agent directly from Slice Settings ("Connect an agent")
or the CLI:

    gs auth create-agent-invite --slice <account>/<slice> --role contributor
    gs auth list-agent-invites
    gs auth revoke-agent-invite <invite-id>

Give the resulting single-use `gsi_...` token (or copyable prompt) to your
agent; it runs `gs onboard --join <gsi_token>` and is immediately owned by you
with slice access granted.

If an agent self-registered with your email instead, open
https://gitslice.io/claims and sign in with an account whose verified email is
exactly the one the agent registered with. Click Accept (or Accept & grant if
the agent requested a slice) to become a co-owner; the agent keeps its access.
From a terminal: `gs auth login`, then `gs claims list` and
`gs claims accept <agent-subject-id>`.

## MCP: hosted HTTP or local stdio (no checkout needed)

Zero-install hosted Streamable HTTP MCP endpoint:

    URL:     https://gitslice.io/mcp?slice=<account>/<slice>
    Headers: Authorization: Bearer <gsk_api_key>
             X-Gitslice-Slice: <account>/<slice>   (optional if ?slice= is set)

Or run locally over stdio with the CLI: `gs mcp --slice <account>/<slice>`.
Tools: read_file, list_directory, search (regex per line, like grep -n),
history, blame, create_changeset (edits: write, delete, move, copy, mkdir;
submit: true submits it), get_changeset and submit_changeset. A submit that
cannot land yet answers status "blocked" with the reason (for example a
required check without a result); call submit_changeset again later. Set
GS_TRACE=/path/trace.jsonl to log every server and tool call as JSON lines.

## Checks and CI

Checks live in `<folder>/.gitslice/checks.yaml`, run on each applicable
patchset, and can be required before `gs submit` accepts a changeset. A check
uses `image` for a container image or `build` to create that image from the
tree; those settings are mutually exclusive. A build accepts `dockerfile`,
`context`, `inputs`, and `timeout`. The daemon rebuilds only when the
Dockerfile or an input changes, and retains the two newest images for each
Dockerfile. Only the Dockerfile and listed inputs are sent to the build, so list
dependency manifests such as `go.mod`, `go.sum`, and `package-lock.json`,
and install dependencies in the image.

    defaults:
      build:
        dockerfile: ci/Dockerfile
        context: "."
        inputs: [go.mod, go.sum, web/package-lock.json]
        timeout: "30m"

Top-level `services` names fresh containers a check can run beside itself. A
service has `image`, `env`, `ready`, `ready_timeout`, and `memory`; a check
selects them with `services: [name]`. Services need a containerized (`image` or
`build`) check. Each run gets a private network and reaches each service at its
name; it is internal unless the check sets `network: true`.

    services:
      postgres:
        image: postgres:16-alpine
        env: { POSTGRES_HOST_AUTH_METHOD: trust }
        ready: "pg_isready -U postgres -h 127.0.0.1"
        ready_timeout: "60s"
        memory: "1g"
    checks:
      e2e:
        build: { dockerfile: ci/Dockerfile, inputs: [go.mod, go.sum] }
        services: [postgres]
        env:
          GITSLICE_TEST_DATABASE_URL: "postgres://postgres@postgres:5432/postgres?sslmode=disable"
        run: "go test ./tests/..."

Containers run as the CI daemon's user. `cache` paths are folders under that
daemon's cache directory.

Run a CI-only daemon on any machine with `gs` and, when checks use `image` or
`build`, Docker or Podman:

    gs auth login
    gs agent doctor --ci
    gs agent install --ci --name my-ci
    gs agent expose my-ci <account>:<slice>

Then a slice owner selects it:

    gs slice set-ci-daemon <account>:<slice> <daemon-id>

A checks-only daemon with nothing to run detaches from the server after two
minutes and polls every 30 seconds for queued checks, so an idle daemon costs
the server almost nothing; a check may start up to about 30 seconds later.
`--detach-after 0` keeps it connected.

Remove its user service with `gs agent uninstall my-ci`. CI-only daemons only
run checks. When the selected CI daemon is offline, its runs stay
queued; the Checks panel and `gs submit` say that checks are waiting for it.

## Secrets

A check that needs a token or key reads it from an environment variable filled
from a secret. A secret belongs to an account and applies to folders of it
(and everything below them); a check gets the secrets at the folder of the
checks.yaml that defines it, and its logs show values of 4 or more characters
as ***. Only the account's owners and admins manage secrets. Pipe values in,
so they stay out of shell history:

    printf %s "$TOKEN" | gs secret create DEPLOY_TOKEN --path /acme/api --path /acme/worker
    printf %s "$TOKEN" | gs secret create NPM_TOKEN --path /acme      # the whole account
    printf %s "$TOKEN" | gs secret create WEB_TOKEN --slice web       # a slice's folders
    gs secret ls
    gs slice secret ls <account>/<slice>     # names that apply in one slice

A folder has one secret per name; where several apply, the closest folder
wins. Anyone who can add a check in a secret's folders can read it from that
check, so choose folders with care. Owners and admins can fill a local env file
whose values are written `NAME=gitslice-secret:SECRET_NAME`, from the secrets
at the template's folder in a workspace (or --path /account/folder):

    gs secret env <account>/<folder>/env.prod.template -o .env.prod

The file is mode 600; no one else can read values. If you are not an owner or
admin, ask one, or work from an example env file without production
credentials.

## Triggers

A trigger runs when files in a folder change. Put `.gitslice/triggers.yaml`
in any folder; changes there or below fire its triggers (and those of the
folders above). An http action posts the event as JSON; a worker action runs
a JavaScript module from the same `.gitslice` folder on Cloudflare, which can
call an outside CI system and report checks that gate submit:

    version: 1
    triggers:
      ci:
        on: [changeset.created, changeset.updated]
        paths: ["**/*.go"]
        checks: [ci]                 # reported as <folder>/ci
        secrets: [GH_TOKEN]
        network: [api.github.com]    # the only hosts the script may reach
        action:
          worker: triggers/ci.js     # exports onEvent(event, gs), onCallback(request, gs)

Definitions come from the target branch head, so a changed trigger takes
effect when it lands; changes under `.gitslice/` need an account owner's or
admin's approval. Inspect runs with `gs trigger ls [folder]`,
`gs trigger runs --changeset <id>`, `gs trigger logs <run-id>`; run one by
hand with `gs trigger run <trigger-id>` (it must list `manual` in `on`).

## Git mirrors (backup to GitHub)

An owner or admin can have the server push a slice to a Git repository
elsewhere, such as GitHub, after every landing and every tag:

    gs slice secret set <account>/<slice> GITHUB_MIRROR_TOKEN < token.txt
    gs slice mirror set <account>/<slice> --url https://github.com/<owner>/<repo>.git \
        --token-secret GITHUB_MIRROR_TOKEN
    gs slice mirror <account>/<slice>          # last push, pending work, last error
    gs slice mirror push <account>/<slice>     # push now
    gs slice mirror rm <account>/<slice>

For GitHub use a fine-grained token with Contents read and write on that one
repository. A slice with one root folder is pushed with that folder as the
repository root. Pushes are fast-forward only: if someone commits on the
remote, the mirror stops and shows the error until the remote is reset.
More: https://gitslice.io/doc/mirrors

## Large slices: lazy workspaces

`gs init` downloads every file of the slice. For a big slice, on Linux or macOS
with FUSE, mount it instead:

    gs init --lazy <account>/<slice> ~/work/<slice>
    cd ~/work/<slice>/<account>/<slice>        # files sit at their full path

It takes seconds (2.6 s for a 4,500-file slice, cold), because only the listing
is fetched. A file is fetched the first time something reads it (with small
files beside it; each first read is a round trip to the server). A walk of the
whole tree (rg, grep -r, a build) is read ahead of; for work that reads
everything, `gs fetch` first is still fastest. Your edits stay on this machine
until `gs create`. Everything else works as in a checkout: `gs status`, `gs diff`,
`gs create`, `gs submit`, `gs sync`, `gs switch`. `gs restore <path>` drops an
edit. `gs checkpoint` saves the edits on this machine (gs also does before
sync, switch, restore and rewind), `gs rewind` goes back to one (and can be
undone the same way), and `gs fork <n> <dir>` opens a checkpoint as a second
workspace. `gs fetch` fetches ahead of time for offline work, and
`gs init --lazy ... --prefetch '<glob>'` fetches matching files in the
background. One background process serves all your lazy workspaces and exits
when the last is unmounted. `gs unmount <dir>` unmounts one, keeping its edits,
and `gs mount <dir>` brings it back (after a reboot too); `gs mount list` shows
them all. When you are done with a workspace, lazy or not,
`gs workspace delete <dir>` removes it from this machine (unmounting a lazy one);
it refuses while there are edits no changeset holds, so `gs create` first or
pass `--force` to discard them. The directory must be empty and not inside
another workspace. Without FUSE, use plain `gs init`.

## Go modules

A slice with one included path is a Go module: `gitslice.io/<account>/<slice>`,
rooted at that path.

- Declare that module path in its go.mod.
- Release with `gs tag create v1.0.0`.
- Consumers run `go get gitslice.io/<account>/<slice>@v1.0.0`.
- For a private slice, add a Gitslice token to ~/.netrc for gitslice.io
  (password: the token) and set GOPRIVATE=gitslice.io/<account>/*.

## Visibility

New slices, including an agent's home slice, are private: only signed-in
members of the account can open them in the browser. `gs browse --print` warns
when a link points at a private slice. To share one:
`gs slice update <account>:<slice> --visibility public`.

## Limits

- Registration is rate limited per client IP (currently 5 per hour).
- The server is `api.gitslice.io:443` by default; pass `--server` to use another.
